channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Former State Police union head sentenced for kickbacks and fraud
item.description: Dana Pullman, former Massachusetts State Police union president, was sentenced to two years for accepting kickbacks and misusing union funds for personal expenses.

item.title: NLRB judge finds Worcester hospital violated nurses’ rights
item.description: NLRB judge finds Saint Vincent Hospital in Worcester committed 14 labor violations against nurses, including withholding bonuses and bypassing union protocols.

item.title: Boston attorney, curler heads to Paralympics
item.description: Anderson & Kreiger attorney Sean O’Neill will compete in wheelchair curling for Team USA at the 2026 Paralympic Games in Italy.

item.title: SCOTUS rejects ‘emergency’ tariffs imposed by Trump
item.description: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled IEEPA does not authorize President Trump to impose tariffs targeting drug trafficking or trade deficits.

item.title: Massachusetts courts issue significant product liability holdings in 2025
item.description: Massachusetts courts issued several important product liability decisions in 2025. Below is a review of the cases and their significant holdings.

item.title: Cases scheduled to be heard in March
item.description: Following is a list of the cases scheduled to be argued before the Supreme Judicial Court in March. The summaries of the issues presented in the cases have been prepared by Lawyers Weekly.

item.title: Judge’s $10K spoliation sanction just doesn’t cut it, attorney says
item.description: Judge awards $10,000 sanction against defendant in TelexFree MDL over spoliation of ESI, rejecting harsher penalties based on claims of intentional misconduct.

item.title: Construction worker trips and falls on narrow, elevated walkway
item.description: The plaintiff brought a negligence suit for injuries he suffered after falling on a narrow, elevated walking-working surface on a construction site on Aug. 30, 2021.

item.title: Roofer falls onto concrete wall, fractures spine
item.description: On April 25, 2024, the claimant was an employee for a subcontractor working on the roof of a house in Keene, New Hampshire, when he fell 10 feet onto a concrete retaining wall. He was flown to UMass Medical Center in Worcester.

item.title: Epilepsy patient suffers TBI during laser brain surgery
item.description: The patient, 43, had a complicated history of medically refractory seizures and could no longer work or drive but was generally living independently in her own home.
